title: AlphaEvolve: A coding agent for scientific and algorithmic discovery

mechanism.domainTask: Scientific and algorithmic discovery through executable-code evolution and code superoptimization
mechanism.populationDetail: A persistent evolutionary program database combines MAP-Elites-inspired diversity preservation with island-based population models, but the exact cell/island organization is not fully disclosed.
mechanism.archiveDetail: The program database is explicitly inspired by MAP-Elites and is intended to preserve diverse high-quality programs for later resurfacing; descriptor-cell admission details are not given.
mechanism.replacementDetail: The database serves simultaneously as reusable population memory and diversity-preserving archive; its implementation is described at a design level rather than with complete admission pseudocode.
mechanism.generationDetail: One sampled parent program is directly edited through structured SEARCH/REPLACE diffs; inspiration programs are contextual references rather than additional true parents.
mechanism.feedbackDetail: Prompts include rendered programs, execution results, and metric scores; optional LLM-generated feedback and multiple score dimensions steer later evolution.
mechanism.parentSelectionDetail: Figure 2 exposes database.sample() returning one parent_program and inspirations; the detailed database sampling and global-vs-island scope are not specified.
mechanism.outOfTaxonomy: A single evolutionary database jointly combines MAP-Elites-style diversity, island-inspired organization, contextual inspiration retrieval, and static Flash/Pro model specialization.

provenance.sourcePdf: papers/AlphaEvolve A coding agent for scientific and algorithmic discovery.pdf
provenance.citationWarning: The current survey places AlphaEvolve under flat populations and quality-diversity archives, but the white paper also explicitly invokes island-based population models. Do not count inspiration programs as true parents. Archive admission/replacement and parent sampling scope are under-specified; model subtype is best read as static role-based assignment rather than dynamic routing.
